children: The yield on Canada's two-year government bond trades at 3.41%, or the highest level in over two years — or July 31, 2024. Back in July of 2024, the Bank of Canada's policy rate was at 4.50%, on a downward trend after taming historically high inflation. The two-year yield is now 50 basis points higher from a low reached in late August, and this reflects growing concern over inflation and the need for higher interest rates. Some economists note the BOC doesn't necessarily need to raise rates given the gap between the policy rate, at 2.25%, and the 2-year yield, because the selloff in the bond market is de facto tightening monetary conditions. (paul.vieira@wsj.com)
